name: mvp-factory
label: MVP Factory — Founders & Product Builders
description: Targets two buyer segments for AOTT's MVP Factory service: (1) founders and entrepreneurs at early-stage companies who have a commercial product idea and need a technical build partner; (2) technical or operational decision-makers at growing companies (10–200 people) who have a repeating manual process they know should be a product but lack the in-house capacity to build it quickly. The classic entry signal is someone doing repetitive work and asking why it is not automated yet. AOTT's proof-of-work is Scorestack, StoreSync, and Bridge — commercial-grade products built with Spec-Driven Development via Claude Code. The pitch is speed-to-market and predictability: from Spec to working product in weeks, not months, with scope defined upfront so there is no drift. This is NOT a staff augmentation pitch — it is a build-partner pitch.
_note: The buyer is always the person who owns the 'build vs buy' decision and has budget authority. Key positive signals: founding a company, leading product or engineering at a lean org (under ~200 people), running operations limited by manual processes or missing tooling, building or planning to build a SaaS product, any mention of repetitive work or manual workarounds that should be automated. The prototypical buyer has seen this pattern in their own work: a repeating process that costs time every week, no internal team to productise it, and a clear sense that 'someone should build a tool for this.' That someone is AOTT. Key negative signals: individual technical contributor (they build it themselves), pure enterprise (internal dev capacity), pure sales/marketing role without build authority, recruiter/staffing (wrong service entirely). Company stage matters more than industry: a Founder at a 5-person company with a clear problem beats a VP at a 5,000-person company every time.
_classifier_note: Do NOT apply an end-client penalty for this criteria. MVP Factory targets both direct product builds (commercial SaaS) and internal tool builds — the buyer is always an end-client, never a subcontracting partner. Score founders at early-stage companies highly even when industry signals are weak. Penalise large-enterprise signals (Fortune 500, publicly traded company with thousands of employees) since they typically have internal dev teams. Reward explicit product-building language in headlines ('building', 'launching', 'co-founder of', 'building [tool]') and ops-limiting language ('manual', 'spreadsheets', 'no system for').
reference_products: Scorestack — LinkedIn enrichment, AI scoring, and outreach automation for sales and RevOps teams
StoreSync — Shopify environment promotion tool for agencies managing dev/staging/production store pairs
Bridge — NetSuite-to-Shopify configuration alignment and migration tool for consultants and merchants
ideal_buyer_profiles: Founder at a pre-seed or seed-stage SaaS company who has a spec or wireframe but no engineering team
CTO or VP Engineering at a 15–100-person company running manual ops workflows that need to be productised
Head of Product at a startup that is outgrowing its no-code stack and needs a custom build
COO or Head of Operations at a services business that needs an internal tool to replace spreadsheets
Solo founder in the Shopify or NetSuite ecosystem building a niche vertical tool
_excluded_employers_note: Employees of large platform vendors and big tech (Oracle, NetSuite, Shopify, Salesforce, SAP, Adobe, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) are never MVP Factory buyers — they have effectively unlimited internal build capacity, the exact opposite of the target profile. Classify cold, cap score at 25, regardless of title. Detect from the headline when company fields are null ('at Oracle', '@ Shopify', etc.). This is the large-enterprise penalty from _classifier_note applied as a hard rule.

Unlike excluded_employers (surfaced cold), these are dropped entirely at Step 2 — skip the result AND write it to seen.json so it never resurfaces. Detect from headline naming the firm; Seibert Consulting Group's staff may abbreviate as 'SCG' in headlines (e.g. 'at SCG') — treat that alongside any Seibert/NetSuite/Shopify Plus context as the same exclusion.
